# Quick add

PROVIDES one-line natural-language task capture SO THAT every surface CAN create a task from a single typed line.

The capability turns a typed line into a task the task domain accepts. It owns interpretation of the line and nothing about how the line is collected or the task rendered.

## Assertions

### Test.Scenario: capture

- [capture-basic](tests/capture-basic.scenario.l1.test.ts):
  - Given the interpreter is up and the list holds no task
  - When a person submits "water plants", then "call mom"
  - Then the list holds exactly two tasks, "water plants" then "call mom", each with no due date
- [capture-fallback](tests/capture-fallback.scenario.l1.test.ts):
  - Given the interpreter is up and returns no parseable result for the line
  - When a person submits "zzq 4ever ~~"
  - Then exactly one new task exists, titled "zzq 4ever ~~", with no due date, labelled "Uninterpreted"
- [outage-fallback](tests/outage-fallback.scenario.l2.test.ts):
  - Given the interpreter accepts the request and never answers
  - When a person submits "call mom tomorrow 5pm"
  - Then within 2 seconds exactly one new task exists, titled "call mom tomorrow 5pm", with no due date, labelled "Uninterpreted"
- [capture-event](tests/capture-event.scenario.l1.test.ts):
  - Given a signed-in person
  - When the person submits a line that creates a task
  - Then exactly one capture event is sent, carrying the person's id and the time of the submission

### Test.Compliance: degraded capture

- [task-under-failure](tests/task-under-failure.compliance.l1.test.ts): ALWAYS: a submitted line yields exactly one new task under every interpretation failure.
- [line-verbatim](tests/line-verbatim.compliance.l1.test.ts): NEVER: the title of a task created under an interpretation failure differs, as a sequence of code points, from the submitted line with Unicode White_Space removed from both ends.
- [reinterpret-later](tests/reinterpret-later.compliance.l1.test.ts): ALWAYS: a task created under an interpretation failure keeps its submitted line, and interpreting it again later sets its title and due date without the person typing the line again.

### Test.Compliance: interpreter fallback

- [fallback-task](tests/fallback-task.compliance.l1.test.ts): ALWAYS: when the model is unreachable or returns no parseable result, quick add creates exactly one task from the deterministic fallback, titled with the line with Unicode White_Space removed from both ends, with no due date, labelled "Uninterpreted".
- [fallback-latency](tests/fallback-latency.compliance.l2.test.ts): NEVER: with the model failing, more than 2 seconds pass from the submission to the task.

### Test.Mapping: [date-phrases](tests/date-phrases.mapping.l1.test.ts)

With the interpreter up and the server running in UTC, a line resolves to its due date as a local date-time in the person's timezone. Each row gives that timezone and the local time of the submission.

| Case           | Timezone         | Submitted at     | Line                          | Due              |
| -------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------- |
| tomorrow-5pm   | Europe/Zurich    | 2026-08-14T10:00 | "call mom tomorrow 5pm"       | 2026-08-15T17:00 |
| absolute-date  | Europe/Zurich    | 2026-08-14T10:00 | "dentist 2026-08-20 9am"      | 2026-08-20T09:00 |
| next-thursday  | Europe/Zurich    | 2026-08-14T10:00 | "dentist thu 9am"             | 2026-08-20T09:00 |
| next-friday    | Pacific/Auckland | 2026-08-11T10:00 | "call mom next friday 5pm"    | 2026-08-14T17:00 |
| tomorrow-nz    | Pacific/Auckland | 2026-08-11T10:00 | "dentist tomorrow 9am"        | 2026-08-12T09:00 |
| in-3-weeks     | Europe/Zurich    | 2026-08-14T10:00 | "renew passport in 3 weeks"   | 2026-09-04T09:00 |
| first-of-month | Europe/Zurich    | 2026-08-14T10:00 | "pay rent first of the month" | 2026-09-01T09:00 |

### Test.Property: local days

- [local-day](tests/local-day.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone and every submission time in it from 1970 to 2100, a line with "tomorrow 9am" gets a due date of 09:00 local time on the next calendar day, a daylight-saving change between the two included.
- [next-weekday](tests/next-weekday.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone, every submission day from 1970 to 2100, and every weekday, "next" with that weekday names the first such weekday after the day of submission.
- [default-time](tests/default-time.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone, every submission time in it from 1970 to 2100, and every line that names a day and no time, the due date is 09:00 local time on the day the line names.

### Test.Conformance: export

- [task-payload](tests/task-payload.conformance.l1.test.ts): Every created task conforms to [the task schema](spx/30-task.domain/contracts/task.schema.json), validated under JSON Schema 2020-12 with format assertion on.

### Evaluate: [parse-quality](evals/parse-quality/eval.toml)

The model path of the interpreter receives the line, the person's timezone, Europe/Zurich, and the submission time, 2026-08-14T10:00. It returns a title and a due date. An output passes a case when its title equals the expected title and its due date names the same local date-time, or both name none. The score of a run is the share of passing outputs over every sample of every case.

| Case         | Line                          | Title            | Due              |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| call-mom     | "call mom tomorrow 5pm"       | "call mom"       | 2026-08-15T17:00 |
| dentist      | "dentist thu 9am"             | "dentist"        | 2026-08-20T09:00 |
| water-plants | "water plants"                | "water plants"   | none             |
| passport     | "renew passport in 3 weeks"   | "renew passport" | 2026-09-04T09:00 |
| rent         | "pay rent first of the month" | "pay rent"       | 2026-09-01T09:00 |

### Audit: messages

- reject-message: ALWAYS: a message about an uninterpreted line names the part not understood, such as the date, and offers exactly one recovery action, such as "Edit date". A message that names no part, or offers no action or two, fails.

### Probe: running capture

- [representative-capture](probes/representative-capture/probe.md): The running product, its clock set to Friday 2026-08-14 at 10:00 in the person's timezone, Europe/Zurich. With the interpreter live, a person submits "water plants", "call mom", and "zzq 4ever ~~". With the interpreter process stopped, the person submits "dentist thu 9am". With the interpreter started again and its process then suspended, so that it accepts each request and never answers, the person submits "call mom tomorrow 5pm" with two spaces before it and one after. With the interpreter live again, the person interprets both tasks again. Covers [capture-basic](quick-add.spec.md#capture-basic), [capture-fallback](quick-add.spec.md#capture-fallback), [outage-fallback](quick-add.spec.md#outage-fallback), [reject-message](quick-add.spec.md#reject-message), [task-under-failure](quick-add.spec.md#task-under-failure), [line-verbatim](quick-add.spec.md#line-verbatim), [reinterpret-later](quick-add.spec.md#reinterpret-later), [fallback-task](quick-add.spec.md#fallback-task), and [fallback-latency](quick-add.spec.md#fallback-latency).

- [local-day](tests/local-day.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone and every submission time in it from 1970 to 2100, a line with "tomorrow 9am" gets a due date of 09:00 local time on the next calendar day, a daylight-saving change between the two included.
- [next-weekday](tests/next-weekday.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone, every submission day from 1970 to 2100, and every weekday, "next" with that weekday names the first such weekday after the day of submission.
- [default-time](tests/default-time.property.l1.test.ts): For every IANA timezone, every submission time in it from 1970 to 2100, and every line that names a day and no time, the due date is 09:00 local time on the day the line names.

### Evaluate: [parse-quality](evals/parse-quality/eval.toml)

The model path of the interpreter receives the line, the person's timezone, Europe/Zurich, and the submission time, 2026-08-14T10:00. It returns a title and a due date. An output passes a case when its title equals the expected title and its due date names the same local date-time, or both name none. The score of a run is the share of passing outputs over every sample of every case.

| Case         | Line                          | Title            | Due              |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| call-mom     | "call mom tomorrow 5pm"       | "call mom"       | 2026-08-15T17:00 |
| dentist      | "dentist thu 9am"             | "dentist"        | 2026-08-20T09:00 |
| water-plants | "water plants"                | "water plants"   | none             |
| passport     | "renew passport in 3 weeks"   | "renew passport" | 2026-09-04T09:00 |
| rent         | "pay rent first of the month" | "pay rent"       | 2026-09-01T09:00 |

### Audit: messages

- reject-message: ALWAYS: a message about an uninterpreted line names the part not understood, such as the date, and offers exactly one recovery action, such as "Edit date". A message that names no part, or offers no action or two, fails. ([audit])

### Probe: running capture

- [representative-capture](probes/representative-capture/probe.md): The running product, its clock set to Friday 2026-08-14 at 10:00 in the person's timezone, Europe/Zurich. With the interpreter live, a person submits "water plants", "call mom", and "zzq 4ever ~~". With the interpreter process stopped, the person submits "dentist thu 9am". With the interpreter started again and its process then suspended, so that it accepts each request and never answers, the person submits "call mom tomorrow 5pm" with two spaces before it and one after. With the interpreter live again, the person interprets both tasks again. Covers [capture-basic](quick-add.spec.md#capture-basic), [capture-fallback](quick-add.spec.md#capture-fallback), [outage-fallback](quick-add.spec.md#outage-fallback), [reject-message](quick-add.spec.md#reject-message), [task-under-failure](quick-add.spec.md#task-under-failure), [line-verbatim](quick-add.spec.md#line-verbatim), [reinterpret-later](quick-add.spec.md#reinterpret-later), [fallback-task](quick-add.spec.md#fallback-task), and [fallback-latency](quick-add.spec.md#fallback-latency).
